blocks.text: As the atomic size increases down a group, the larger electron cloud makes the incoming electron feel less attraction from the nucleus, so electron affinity generally decreases down the group; among the halogens the order is At less than I less than Br less than F less than Cl. Across a period electron affinities generally become more negative from left to right, first because the nuclear charge increases and attracts additional electrons more strongly, and second because the atomic radius decreases.

blocks.caption: Electron affinities for group 1 and group 17, kJ per mol (Table 1.1)

blocks.alt: Left: a grid of main-group elements of periods 1 to 4 with their Pauling electronegativity values, from 0.8 for potassium and rubidium to 4.0 for fluorine, with arrows showing the increase across a period and up a group. Right: the electron affinities of group 17 and group 1 as a two-column table with notes on the sign, the second electron affinity and the trends.
blocks.caption: Electronegativity values and the electron affinities of groups 1 and 17 (original diagram after Figure 1.8 and Table 1.1).
blocks.long_description: Electron affinity becomes more negative across a period, from -60 kJ per mol for lithium to -328 for fluorine, as the nuclear charge rises and the atom shrinks, and less negative down a group, from -349 for chlorine to -270.1 for astatine, as the atom grows. Fluorine's value (-328) is less negative than chlorine's (-349) because its very small 2p shell repels the incoming electron. The electronegativity grid on the left follows the same directions, from under 1 for the alkali metals to 4.0 for fluorine.

blocks.prompt: Fluorine is smaller than chlorine, yet its electron affinity (-328 kJ per mol) is less negative than chlorine's (-349). Explain.
blocks.explanation: Smaller size normally means a stronger pull on the incoming electron, but fluorine's 2p subshell is so compact that the electrons already there repel the newcomer strongly, which offsets the attraction. Chlorine's larger 3p subshell has room, so it releases more energy.

items: Electron affinity decreases (less negative) down a group as atoms grow (At less than I less than Br less than F less than Cl) and becomes more negative across a period (more nuclear charge, smaller radius).
Table 1.1: halogens -270 to -349 kJ per mol; alkali metals -46 to -60 kJ per mol.
